findings.title: Durable I/O failure paths have no fault-injection regression coverage
findings.evidence: Append handles partial/zero writes and file Sync failures by degrading; create handles parent Sync failure. No current tests inject these failures or assert restart/supervisor behavior after an uncertain durable append.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a narrow injectable file/sync abstraction and test zero-byte write, partial write, file Sync failure, and parent-directory Sync failure. Assert the writer becomes unusable, does not append another event or create a replacement chain, and recovery fails closed or derives only the fully durable chain according to the supervisor contract.

resolved: BE-CODE-1: creation and recovery are separated; missing and empty recovery sidecars reject; POSIX parent directory Sync is present.
BE-CODE-2: commit attempts are bounded and attempt 2 terminal failure is covered by a full append/close/reopen chain.
BE-CODE-3: later events remain bound to known plan and bundle HMAC values, including terminal events.
BE-CODE-4: a valid attempt_started fixture now reaches the pre-write capacity guard and verifies unchanged file length plus degraded state.
integration_gates: Coordinator/HTTP harness and pilot_e2e wiring remain absent from reviewed files.
Supervisor must enforce cross-process per-case lifecycle locking and current catalog reauthorization.
Pass OpenVerified handles/identity and enforce Windows ACL plus parent-directory durability before integration.
Cleanup, WAL/SHM/journal lifecycle, and full §94 end-to-end recovery acceptance remain unverified here.
